newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia confirms 10-yr global bond issue.
newsitem.headline: Colombia confirms 10-yr global bond issue.

text.p: A senior finance ministry official confirmed reports that Colombia will launch a $750 million 10-year global bond next week, saying the issue was part of the $1.4 billion in sovereign debt the country plans to sell this year.
The $750 million bond will be launched simultaneously in the United States, Europe and Asia, Clemente del Valle, the ministry's chief of Public Credit, told Reuters.
He spoke after an official at joint lead manager J.P. Morgan announced the bond issue in London. Merrill Lynch is the other joint lead manager.
Colombia's central bank has authorized the government to issue up to $1.8 billion in bonds this year but Del Valle said the finance ministry plans to issue no more than $1.4 billion.
He declined to speculate about possible spreads on the $750 million global bond. A $400 million five-year Eurobond was launched by Colombia last May at 150 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes.
Del Valle said the lastest bond issue was likely to be completed by the middle of next week.

The flotation will come less than a month before Washington will announce whether or not Colombia should remain on a virtual "blacklist" of countries that have failed to participate actively enough in the anti-drug fight.

So-called "decertification" for a second consecutive year could trigger economic sanctions that the administration of U.S. President Bill Clinton fell short of imposing in 1996. Sanctions would likely include increased tariffs on Colombian exports to the United States.

But Clinton could invoke the International Emergency Economic Powers Act to impose a wide variety of punitive measures, including the suspension of banking services between the United States and Colombia.
